newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech coalition partners agree budget support - CTK.
newsitem.headline: Czech coalition partners agree budget support - CTK.

text.p: Partners in the centre-right Czech ruling coalition said on Thursday they had reached a compromise to enable their full support for the government's draft 1997 budget, the Czech CTK agency reported.

It quoted leaders of the three parties as saying that a compromise with the junior Civic Democratic Alliance (ODA), dealing mainly with plans to deregulate energy and housing prices, would enable the coalition parties to support the budget. The budget is expected to go to a final vote on Friday.
Details of the compromise were not immediately available.
ODA had demanded that the coalition agree to a deregulation plan by 2000, the end of the government's current term.

The head of ODA's caucus in parliament, Ivan Masek, said on Wednesday that the party would vote for the budget "only providing this coalition binds itself to bring to an end the transformation by the end of the term."
The budget, which completed its second reading on Wednesday, plans balanced expenditure and revenue totalling 549.1 billion crowns in 1997 after 491 billion crowns this year.
The government said on Wednesday, however, that this year's budget, which was approved as a balanced budget, may end with a deficit totalling 1.2 billion crowns.

The cabinet froze selected spending in December and will require early repayment from the state-managed deposit insurance fund on some state credits in order to keep the 1996 deficit from growing to between 3.2-5.2 billion crowns.
